name: Jeremiah Wadsworth
bio: a Delegate and a Representative from Connecticut; born in Hartford, Conn., July 12, 1743; attended the common schools; went to sea in 1761; became first mate of a vessel and subsequently master; served in the Revolutionary War as deputy and commissary general; Delegate to the Confederation Congress, 1788; member of the Connecticut ratification convention in 1788; elected as a Pro-Administration candidate to the First Congress (March 4, 1789-March 3, 1791); elected to the Second Congress by special election to fill the vacancy created when United States Representative-elect Pierpont Edwards did not take his seat in the Second Congress; reelected to the succeeding Congress (December 16, 1790-March 3, 1795); was not a candidate for reelection; member of the Connecticut state house of representatives in 1795; member of the Connecticut state executive council, 1795-1801; engaged in agricultural pursuits; died in Hartford, Conn., April 30, 1804; interment in Ancient Burying Ground.
